reasons.DATE-TYPE: Univer returns a date as its day number and attaches a date format only to DATE/DATEVALUE-style results; it is the same day. The cell's own format shows it, and the exported formula is identical, so Excel formats it the same way.
reasons.BLANK-ZERO: A formula that points at an empty cell: Excel and Univer say 0, the older engine showed nothing. Excel is the spec.
reasons.ARITY: Too few arguments: Excel refuses to accept the formula, and the two engines name different errors. Cannot occur in a workbook Excel could have written.
reasons.UNIVER-MORE: Univer (like Excel) evaluates this; the older engine returned an error (whole-column references, 2-D INDEX, arrays inside SUMPRODUCT, text counted as 0 by AVERAGEA).
reasons.CIRCULAR: A circular reference: Univer (like Excel) calculates 0, the older engine said #CIRC!. Said out loud now: the evaluator lists the cells (circular), the grid shows a notice after the calculation, and the exports append the same notice.
reasons.NAME-SCOPE: A name defined on one sheet and used on another: Univer resolves it (workbook-wide, which is what the Excel file writes); the older engine kept it to its own sheet and said #NAME?.
reasons.OVERFLOW: Numeric overflow edge: Excel answers #NUM!; the engines differ in what they answer. Not reachable by an ordinary model.
reasons.SPILL: A range where one value is expected: Excel spills it into the neighbouring cells (#SPILL! when they are occupied); the older engine said #VALUE!.
reasons.DATEDIF-MD: DATEDIF with "md" — Microsoft documents it as unreliable; the engines differ.
